g1.label: 1. What was the narrator's first reaction to the racist chanting during the match?
g1.why: The text says her hands were shaking by half-time as the chanting continued.

g2.label: 2. Who did the narrator tell first about what had happened?
g2.why: The coach noticed something was wrong and asked, and the narrator told her everything before the referee was informed.

g3.correct: It contacted a local anti-discrimination charity
accept: It contacted a local anti-discrimination charity
g3.label: 3. What did the club do after the game?
g3.why: The text says the club got in touch with a local anti-discrimination charity that visits schools and clubs.

g4.correct: Two fans were banned and a new reporting system was introduced
accept: Two fans were banned and a new reporting system was introduced
g4.label: 4. What had changed six months after the incident, according to the text?
g4.why: The final part of paragraph 3 says two fans had been banned and the league had introduced a new reporting system.

g5.correct: It is a gerund acting as the subject of the sentence
accept: It is a gerund acting as the subject of the sentence
g5.label: 5. In "Reporting racist incidents matters more than people often realise", what job does "Reporting" do?
g5.why: "Reporting" is the -ing form of a verb used as a noun — it is what "matters", so it is the subject of the sentence, not the main verb (which is "matters").

g6.label: 6. (Review) This account of the incident is written from which point of view?
g6.why: Review from 10g-short-story-analysis: the narrator speaks as "I" throughout ("I still remember...", "my hands were shaking"), which marks first-person narration.

g1.label: 1. ___ discrimination in sport should be everyone's responsibility, not just the referee's.
g1.why: A gerund can act as the subject of a sentence — "Reporting" (not the base form "Report" or the infinitive "To report") is the standard subject form here.

g2.label: 2. The whole team is committed to ___ against racism at every match.
g2.why: "Committed to" is followed by a gerund, because "to" here is a preposition, not part of an infinitive — compare "good at fighting", "keen on fighting".

g3.label: 3. Instead of ___ silent, Amara told her coach exactly what had happened.
g3.why: "Instead of" is a preposition, and a gerund always follows a preposition — "staying", not the base form "stay" or the past form "stayed".

g4.label: 4. The charity is responsible for ___ workshops in local schools and clubs.
g4.why: "Responsible for" is followed by a gerund because "for" is a preposition — "organising", not the infinitive "to organise".

g5.label: 5. ___ up against injustice takes real courage, especially in front of a crowd.
g5.why: As the subject of the sentence, the -ing form is needed — "Standing up", not the base form "Stand" or the infinitive "To stand".

g6.label: 6. After ___ the incident, the referee spoke to both team captains.
g6.why: "After" is a preposition here, so it takes a gerund — "reporting", not the base form "report" or the infinitive "to report".

g7.label: 7. The club is proud of ___ a zero-tolerance policy this season.
g7.why: "Proud of" is followed by a gerund because "of" is a preposition — "introducing", not the infinitive "to introduce".

g8.label: 8. Without ___ their voices, fans and players cannot help change the culture of the game.
g8.why: "Without" is a preposition and takes a gerund — "raising" (a transitive verb meaning to lift something up), not "rise" (intransitive, cannot take an object like "their voices") or the base form "raise".

g1.label: 1. The coach suggested ___ (organise) a diversity workshop for the whole team.
g1.why: "Suggest" is always followed by a gerund, never a to-infinitive — "suggested organising", not "suggested to organise".

g2.label: 2. Amara promised ___ (speak) to the team about what had happened.
g2.why: "Promise" is followed by a to-infinitive — "promised to speak", not the gerund "speaking".

g3.label: 3. Many fans can't stand ___ (see) racist abuse go unpunished.
g3.why: "Can't stand" behaves like other feeling verbs (enjoy, hate) and is followed by a gerund — "seeing", not the infinitive "to see".

g4.label: 4. The club decided ___ (introduce) a stronger reporting system after the incident.
g4.why: "Decide" is followed by a to-infinitive — "decided to introduce", not the gerund "introducing".

g5.label: 5. We should avoid ___ (ignore) small incidents, because they can grow into bigger problems.
g5.why: "Avoid" is always followed by a gerund, never a to-infinitive — "avoid ignoring", not "avoid to ignore".

g6.label: 6. The rival team agreed ___ (support) Amara publicly after the match.
g6.why: "Agree" is followed by a to-infinitive — "agreed to support", not the gerund "supporting".

g7.label: 7. I really enjoy ___ (help) younger players feel safe and included at training.
g7.why: "Enjoy" is always followed by a gerund, never a to-infinitive — "enjoy helping", not "enjoy to help".

g8.label: 8. The league plans ___ (launch) a new anti-discrimination campaign next season.
g8.why: "Plan" is followed by a to-infinitive — "plans to launch", not the gerund "launching".
